data.title: Crowd Sourcing Broken QR Codes
data.author: devmandan
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一项免费修复无法扫描的QR码的服务。用户可以通过提交表单或邮件发送损坏的QR码，作者将尝试修复并将其加入数据集，以改进QR码修复技术。作者分享了一次成功修复猫咪项圈上磨损QR码的经历，并提到与Greg合作探讨QR码失败模式的经历。作者希望通过手动修复收集到的损坏QR码，逐步实现可靠的自动修复工具，并呼吁用户提交真实无法扫描的QR码以帮助改进技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：QR码的修复、使用及其失败模式的分析

不同观点：
• myself248和impune提到了QrazyBox工具，认为它是一个可以手动修复损坏QR码的有效工具，尽管存在一定限制。
• nayuki和devmandan强调了手动修复QR码的必要性，并建议通过收集损坏的QR码进行分析和修复实验，以找到可靠的修复方法。nayuki还推荐了QrazyBox工具。
• ethan_smith指出QR码内置的Reed-Solomon错误校正功能已经提供了不同级别的容错能力，因此即使部分损坏或遮挡，QR码通常仍能被读取。
• OtherShrezzing补充说明QR码的元数据和重复数据结构，认为修复元数据部分和迭代版本号可以使大多数损坏的QR码重新可用。
• irs分享了参与QR Show的经历，表示这一经历改变了对QR码的看法，并提供了相关链接。

补充讨论：
• Retr0id提到QR码由于附着在非平面上而导致的失败模式，并建议利用AI和LIDAR技术来自动纠正这些情况。
• viiralvx讨论了QR码与条形码的比较，提出是否可以在QR码中加入类似条形码的文本编码以识别损坏的码，并对是否能在一个方形中合理显示提出疑问。
• ForHackernews指出一个常见问题：即使QR码本身完好，但如果其链接的服务停止付费或失效，扫描结果也会失败。
• technotarek的评论与主讨论点无关，属于幽默插入，问及“丢失的猫”的结局。

争议焦点：
• QR码修复的可靠方法：是依赖内置的错误校正功能（ethan_smith的观点），还是通过手动修复和模式分析（nayuki和devmandan的观点）来实现更有效的修复。

43914321.article_content:
Photo by
傅甬 华
/
Unsplash
Is your QR code not scanning? You've come to the right place!
Submit Your Broken QR Code for a Free Repair
Upload your non‑scanning QR code now:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdn3K9KEV72LPhPPzfS8YvBBzBeoYLbi5cB7IjlQHfsn2xtMg/viewform?usp=header
You can also optionally email it to me at:
daniel@humanqr.com
.
I’ll try to repair your QR code and send you the results. Your code will also join a dataset we’re building to improve QR‑code restoration. Once we’ve collected and fixed enough samples, we’ll release the dataset so others can keep advancing a solution that wouldn't need to be done by hand.
Background Story
Awhile ago someone said their friend found a stray cat outside of their home. It had an electronic tag that had a QR code on it. They reached out to me because the QR code was worn out and wouldn't scan. They sent a photo of the QR code and asked if I could try repairing it.
The QR code was badly worn down from jostling back and forth on the cat's collar.
So I went ahead and tried to repair the QR code:
The repair process for this one involved isolating the code and increasing the contrast.
It also involved fixing the corner.
To even my own surprise, I was able to fix it and it scanned.
Many months later,
Greg
, who I hadn't met at the time, was wondering why a QR code he stumbled across didn't scan. Greg's curiosity led to a conversation that resulted in putting on a
QR show
. I happened to hear about the event and attended.
The show was a ton of fun and I got into some great conversations about QR codes.
Greg and I got into a conversation at one point. I had asked about what made them put on the event. Greg had explained that he too had come across a broken QR code.
Greg had suggested QR codes have failure modes but not enough is known as to why a QR code doesn't scan when it fails to scan.
You'll know
when the QR code scans
.
You know
when the QR code is not scanning
.
You
w
on't know why or how
it failed to scan.
There isn't any in-between. It's very all-or-nothing.
I'd shared with Greg my own story of fixing one up and we had discussed a software tool should exist to repair QR codes as being something that people could really benefit from because QR codes are used everywhere.
I'd like to find a way to repair QR codes in a reliable way. However, that begins with collecting a bunch of broken and corrupted QR codes people stumble across and fixing them up by hand. So please help out by submitting your QR code that doesn't scan. Please don't create QR codes that don't scan just to submit them. Thank you!

主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）对编程工作和知识工作者的未来影响

不同观点：
• gardnr认为，尽管未来会非常不同，但仍需要程序员来审查代码并确保方向正确。AI可能替代大量人工，尤其是可以通过键盘、视频和鼠标完成的工作，预计2025到2030年知识工作将崩溃。
• idiotsecant强调编程是一项 skilled trade，应当组织工会以应对资本剥削。他批评那些认为仅通过学习Python就能获得高薪的人，并认为这种观点在当前环境下不切实际。
• StefanBatory预测初级编程职位将大量减少，未来只需要经验丰富、能力强的开发者，普通的开发者将不再被需要。他还提到，类似于《The Mythical Man-Month》一书中的开发模式可能会回归，且前端开发者可能会因其在UI/UX方面的专长而保持价值。
• 90d对单一高级工程师加LLM能替代2-4名初级工程师的观点持怀疑态度，认为这种模式可能会产生大量问题（slop）。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI对编程工作的替代程度以及对不同层次程序员的影响。部分评论者认为高级开发者将依然重要，而初级职位将面临严重冲击。
• idiotsecant还提出了程序员工会化的必要性，暗示当前行业对普通开发者的保护不足。
• 讨论中引用了《The Mythical Man-Month》中的开发模式作为历史参考，表明对未来开发模式的预测可能需要借鉴过去的经验。

data.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-Play Reasoning with Zero Data
data.author: leodriesch
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种新的强化学习范式，称为"Absolute Zero"（绝对零点），该模型无需任何外部数据，通过自我生成任务并解决这些任务来提升推理能力。传统方法依赖人类标注的数据集，但该方法通过自我演化训练课程和使用代码执行器验证答案，实现了无监督的学习。实验表明，Absolute Zero Reasoner (AZR) 在编码和数学推理任务上表现出色，超越了依赖大量人类标注数据的现有模型。该方法适用于不同规模和类型的模型，展示了在无数据条件下提升AI推理能力的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自生成数据和自 play 技术在模型训练中的应用及其效果的讨论

不同观点：
• a2128 指出该模型并非在零数据情况下训练，而是基于一个在大规模数据（18万亿tokens）上预训练的模型（Qwen 2.5），并通过结合Python解释器的自生成数据进行微调。这表明预训练数据和自生成数据的结合可能是有效的。

Title:
Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data, by Andrew Zhao and 10 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has shown promise in enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models by learning directly from outcome-based rewards. Recent RLVR works that operate under the zero setting avoid supervision in labeling the reasoning process, but still depend on manually curated collections of questions and answers for training. The scarcity of high-quality, human-produced examples raises concerns about the long-term scalability of relying on human supervision, a challenge already evident in the domain of language model pretraining. Furthermore, in a hypothetical future where AI surpasses human intelligence, tasks provided by humans may offer limited learning potential for a superintelligent system. To address these concerns, we propose a new RLVR paradigm called Absolute Zero, in which a single model learns to propose tasks that maximize its own learning progress and improves reasoning by solving them, without relying on any external data. Under this paradigm, we introduce the Absolute Zero Reasoner (AZR), a system that self-evolves its training curriculum and reasoning ability by using a code executor to both validate proposed code reasoning tasks and verify answers, serving as an unified source of verifiable reward to guide open-ended yet grounded learning. Despite being trained entirely without external data, AZR achieves overall SOTA performance on coding and mathematical reasoning tasks, outperforming existing zero-setting models that rely on tens of thousands of in-domain human-curated examples. Furthermore, we demonstrate that AZR can be effectively applied across different model scales and is compatible with various model classes.

data.title: Insurers launch cover for losses caused by AI chatbot errors
data.author: jmacd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在责任和保险中的应用及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [tomrod] 引用的链接内容讨论了AI被用于某种"责任保险"（Accountability insurance）的概念，即当某人未能履行其责任时，由于拥有这种保险，他们可以免于承担后果。这种保险可能导致道德风险，因为个人可能不再对其行为的后果负责。

• [conartist6] 认为这种"责任保险"是不合理的。他通过一个假设的例子说明了问题：如果一个人本应照顾孩子却选择了去喝酒，并将孩子交给AI照顾，结果房子烧毁了，这个人却因为有保险而不需承担责任，这会造成不负责任的行为泛滥。

• [Neywiny] 分享了自己与AI打交道的实际经验，指出AI在处理公寓搜索时自作主张，提供了不准确的信息。他庆幸当时还有人类工作人员在场，避免了潜在的问题。

补充讨论：
• AI在不同情境中的应用可能导致的问题，尤其是在涉及责任和道德判断的领域，如儿童看护和保险。
• 对AI在实际生活中的可靠性和准确性提出质疑，强调了人类监督和干预的重要性。
• 争议的焦点在于AI在责任分担中的角色以及可能引发的道德和伦理问题。

data.title: VMware perpetual license holders receive cease-and-desist letters from Broadcom
data.author: stalfosknight
data.article_summary: Broadcom has been sending cease-and-desist letters to owners of VMware perpetual licenses with expired support contracts, demanding they stop using any software updates or maintenance releases. After acquiring VMware, Broadcom ended perpetual license sales and now requires users to switch to more expensive subscription bundles, with costs rising by up to 300%. Some customers, even those no longer using VMware, have received these letters and faced potential audits. The move has led to backlash, with customers and partners complaining about the increased costs and aggressive enforcement, potentially damaging Broadcom's reputation.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VMware在Broadcom收购后的变化及其对用户的影响，包括价格上涨、许可证问题以及用户迁移选项。

不同观点：
• **Imglorp** 认为，供应商能够大幅提高价格并威胁起诉客户而不影响其股价，说明客户被深度锁定。同时，提出成立专门帮助客户迁移虚拟机的咨询团队可能是个机会。

• **EADDRINUSE** 提到，看到社区资金因Broadcom取消永久许可证并强制提升9.5倍的费用而流失，认为这种行为是违法的。

• **dismalpedigree** 推测VMware可能会在不久的将来与Oracle合并，因为两者采用几乎相同的战术。

• **udev4096** 建议企业迁移到Proxmox或Incus，因为它们是开源的，并且提供企业计划，费用比VMware低得多。

• **NBJack** 提到，曾听说Broadcom会掏空VMware，但实际情况似乎更糟。并提到Broadcom的根源在Hewlett-Packard，所以这种行为并不令人惊讶。

• **polski-g** 描述了VMware被收购后的糟糕情况，包括互联网上的链接失效、论坛和手册消失，以及Broadcom因用户数据库迁移失败而无法销售新许可证，这些都是可避免的错误。

• **dark-star** 认为，对于支持合同到期的客户，不允许使用或安装新补丁是合理的。如果你选择无支持运行，那也可以，但不应安装新补丁。

• **ImJamal** 关心Spring（由VMware拥有）的未来发展。

• **sam_goody** 提到VMware的产品现在可以免费下载，但对于文章中提到的昂贵许可费用和审计权利感到困惑，不清楚哪些产品需要许可。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对Broadcom的策略和VMware的变化反应强烈，尤其是价格上涨和许可证问题。
• 一些用户（如udev4096和dismalpedigree）提出了迁移到其他平台的建议和可能性。
• 对Spring框架的未来表示关注，表明用户不仅关心VMware本身，还关心其拥有的其他技术产品。
• 总体上，用户对VMware在Broadcom收购后的变化感到不满，并积极寻找替代方案和解决办法。

Broadcom has been sending cease-and-desist letters to owners of VMware perpetual licenses with expired support contracts, Ars Technica has confirmed.
Following its November 2023 acquisition of VMware,
Broadcom ended VMware perpetual license sales
. Users with perpetual licenses can still use the software they bought, but they are unable to renew support services
unless they had a pre-existing contract
enabling them
to do so
. The controversial move aims to push VMware users to buy subscriptions to VMware product bundles, with associated costs that have increased by
300 percent
or, in some cases,
more
.
Some customers have opted to continue using VMware unsupported, often as they
research alternatives
, such as VMware rivals or devirtualization.
Over the past weeks, some users running VMware unsupported have
reported
receiving cease-and-desist letters from Broadcom informing them that their contract with VMware and, thus, their right to receive support services, has expired. The letter [
PDF
], reviewed by Ars Technica and signed by Broadcom managing director Michael Brown, tells users that they are to stop using any maintenance releases/updates, minor releases, major releases/upgrades extensions, enhancements, patches, bug fixes, or security patches, save for zero-day security patches, issued since their support contract ended.
The letter tells users that the implementation of any such updates “past the Expiration Date must be immediately removed/deinstalled," adding:
Any such use of Support past the Expiration Date constitutes a material breach of the Agreement with VMware and an infringement of VMware’s intellectual property rights, potentially resulting in claims for enhanced damages and attorneys’ fees.
Some customers of
Members IT Group
, a managed services provider (MSP) in Canada, have received this letter, despite not receiving VMware updates since their support contracts expired, CTO Dean Colpitts told Ars. One customer, he said, received a letter six days after their support contract expired.
Similarly, users online have
reported
receiving cease-and-desist letters even though they haven't issued updates since losing VMware support. One user on Spiceworks’ community forum
reported
receiving such a letter even though they migrated off of VMware and to Proxmox.
Some users who reported receiving a letter from Broadcom said they ended up getting legal teams involved. Ars has also seen confusion online, with some people thinking that the letter means Broadcom perceives that they've broken their agreement with VMware. However, it seems that Broadcom is sending these letters to companies soon after their support contracts have expired, regardless of whether they continue to use (or not use) VMware.
Broadcom didn't respond to a request for comment.
Broadcom warns of potential audits
The cease-and-desist letters also tell recipients that they could be subject to auditing.
Failure to comply with [post-expiration reporting] requirements may result in a breach of the Agreement by Customer[,] and VMware may exercise its right to audit Customer as well as any other available contractual or legal remedy.
In response, Colpitts told Ars:
"The one thing that does kind of piss me off is the fact that Broadcom retains the right to still perform audits whenever they choose. But ... that's utter BS anyways. If a customer wanted to hide stuff, it could easily be done (disclaimer: I have never done this, but since it's all self-reporting in clear text with no security checksums or anything to detect tampering, it would be easy to do)."
Since Broadcom ended VMware's perpetual licenses and increased pricing, numerous users and channel partners, especially small- to medium-size companies, have had to reduce or end business with VMware. Most of Members IT Group’s VMware customer base is now running VMware unsupported. The MSP's biggest concern there is ensuring that staff don't accidentally apply patches to customers, Colpitts noted.
In recent months, Broadcom has sought to rein in potential use of VMware products that it considers unwarranted. For example, it engaged in a since-resolved
legal battle with AT&T
over the telecom’s right to renew support services and has accused
Siemens of pirating VMware software
.
Broadcom’s changes to how VMware is distributed have resulted in various firms ditching VMware and doubting Broadcom's care for customers. While
Broadcom’s financial success
since acquiring VMware suggests that its business plan will remain steadfast, sending cease-and-desist letters to VMware users risks further harming its reputation with current and former customers.
Scharon Harding
Senior Technology Reporter
Scharon Harding
Senior Technology Reporter
Scharon is a Senior Technology Reporter at Ars Technica writing news, reviews, and analysis on consumer gadgets and services.

data.article_summary: 前苹果设计师乔尼·艾夫（Jony Ive）在接受Stripe采访时表示，他的新产品专注于解决iPhone等智能手机带来的“意外后果”，如对用户的负面影响。艾夫强调，创新常伴有不可预见的后果，设计者需对此负责。自2019年离开苹果后，艾夫与OpenAI合作开发新设备，该设备由其设计公司LoveFrom主导，并有原iPhone设计师参与。艾夫还对AI安全表示关注，认为当前对AI的担忧是必要的，与当年社交媒体缺乏讨论形成对比。尽管新产品的具体细节仍未公开，但据报道，该设备将超越传统软件功能，利用AI带来更多用户价值。

不同观点：
• **multimoon** 认为该高管在苹果期间做了许多糟糕的决策，他的离开使苹果产品变得更好。该评论者对他的挣扎感到高兴，暗示他过去对苹果的产品决策产生了负面影响。

• **Gualdrapo** 扩展了 multimoon 的观点，指出该高管的设计决策导致了苹果产品的不可修复性、计划报废和负面环境影响，批评他的设计更多是为了追求美学和个人声誉，而非实际功能或可持续性。

• **petepete** 对该高管目前的工作持怀疑态度，认为所谓的“神秘项目”可能只是新闻噱头，实际上并没有太多实质内容。

• **vanattab** 简单地用“狡猾”来形容该高管，暗示对他个人品德或职业操守的负面评价。

• **casey2** 以讽刺的口吻提到该高管曾声称自己“发明了iPhone”，质疑他的自我宣传和实际贡献。

补充讨论：
- 评论中存在对该高管过去在苹果工作的批评，特别是对他设计的产品的可持续性和环境影响的关注。
- 争议的焦点在于该高管对苹果的实际贡献和其离开后苹果产品的改进之间的关系。一些评论者认为他的离开对苹果产生了积极影响，而其他人则对他的自我宣传和职业操守提出质疑。
- 还有一些评论对该高管目前的工作和项目持怀疑态度，认为可能只是为了吸引注意力而没有实际价值。

43952851.article_content:
News
Jony Ive’s next product is driven by the ‘unintended consequences’ of the iPhone
Ive confirmed last year that he’s working on a new product with OpenAI.
Ive confirmed last year that he’s working on a new product with OpenAI.
by
Emma Roth
May 9, 2025, 2:02 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Screenshot: Stripe via YouTube
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
Former Apple designer Jony Ive says the work on his next product is driven by owning the “unintended consequences” associated with the iPhone. During
an interview with Stripe
, Ive said there’s “not anything that I can be more preoccupied or bothered by” than the potentially adverse effects smartphones have on their users.
“I think when you’re innovating, of course, there will be unintended consequences,” Ive said. “You hope that the majority will be pleasant surprises. Certain products that I’ve been very, very involved with, I think there were some unintended consequences that were far from pleasant.”
Ive spent more than two decades at Apple, where he led the design of many products, including the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and iPod.
He left the company in 2019
to co-found the design firm LoveFrom. Ive confirmed last year that he’s
working on a new device with OpenAI
, which he seemed to allude to during this interview.
“I think even if you’re innocent in your intention, I think if you’re involved in something that has poor consequences, you need to own it,” Ive said. “That ownership, personally, has driven a lot of what I’ve been working on that I can’t talk about the moment, but look forward to being able to talk about at some point in the future.”
When talking about AI, Ive mentioned that he finds it encouraging that “it’s very rare for there to be a discussion about AI, and there not to be the appropriate concerns about safety.” He adds that he was “extremely concerned about social media, and there was no discussion whatsoever.”
Details about what Ive is working on with OpenAI are still slim,
but
The New York Times
reported
that LoveFrom is leading the device’s design with Tang Tan and Evans Hankey, who helped design the iPhone. Ive and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have reportedly discussed how AI has allowed them to create a new device “because the technology could do more for users than traditional software.”

data.title: Anylinuxfs – macOS mount any Linux filesystem read/write using NFS and a microVM
data.author: josephscott
data.article_summary: **anylinuxfs** 是一个允许 macOS 用户通过 NFS 和微型虚拟机读写任何 Linux 支持的文件系统的工具。传统上，macOS 对第三方文件系统的支持有限，依赖于如 macFUSE 等方案。而 **anylinuxfs** 通过启动一个微型虚拟机，使用真实的 Linux 驱动，支持从 ext* 到 btrfs 等文件系统，并允许自定义挂载选项。该工具利用 Alpine Linux 镜像，初次运行时会下载并设置环境，后续操作只需几秒。当前限制包括一次只能挂载一个驱动器，且仅支持 Apple Silicon Macs。该项目基于 **libkrun** 等技术构建。

anylinuxfs
macOS: mount any linux-supported filesystem read/write using NFS and a microVM
Installation
brew tap nohajc/anylinuxfs
brew install anylinuxfs
Demo
anylinuxfs-demo.mov
Introduction
Mounting 3rd-party filesystems on macOS has always been tricky. There's official support for reading NTFS but otherwise we've mainly used solutions based on macFUSE.
We've got NTFS-3g which is a pretty mature driver but for Linux filesystems there's only a couple of experimental solutions like
fuse-ext2
or
ext4fuse
.
If you want a reliable solution with write access, you need to run a Linux virtual machine with physical disk access and take care of exposing the mounted filesystem to the host.
This is exactly what
anylinuxfs
does and it streamlines it so that it's as easy as running one command in terminal.
You pick a drive, mount it with
anylinuxfs
and it appears as a NFS share on localhost. This spins up a microVM in the background which uses the real linux drivers, so you can access anything from
ext*
to
btrfs
. Any mount options on the command-line will be forwarded to the linux mount command, so you can mount read-only, read-write, pick btrfs subvolumes, etc. Then you simply eject the drive in Finder or use
umount
in terminal and the virtual machine will be turned off.
This all sounds like a lot of work but it's actually very fast. Not like a traditional virtual machine which takes a while to boot.
This one is just a stripped down version of Linux, there's not even a UEFI firmware. Practically, it takes only a couple of seconds before the drive is mounted and ready to use.
Notes
When you first run
anylinuxfs
to mount a drive, it will download the alpine Linux image from Docker hub and unpack it to your user profile (
~/.anylinuxfs/alpine
).
Then it will spin up a VM so it can install dependencies and do the initial environment setup. After that, the Linux root filesystem will be reused for every mount operation.
You can also run
anylinuxfs init
to download a fresh copy of
alpine:latest
and reinitialize the environment at any time.
It is needed to run mount commands with
sudo
otherwise we're not allowed direct access to
/dev/disk*
files. However, the virtual machine itself will in fact run under the regular user who invoked
sudo
in the first place (i.e. all unnecessary permissions are dropped after the disk is opened)
Limitations
Only one drive can be mounted at a time (this might be improved in the future)
Only Apple Silicon Macs are supported (libkrun limitation)
Acknowledgements
This project was made possible by
libkrun
the microVM hypervisor for Linux anc Mac
libkrunfw
- Linux kernel bundled for libkrun as a dynamic library
gvproxy
- user space networking for virtual machines (also used by podman)
docker-nfs-server
- launcher for NFS server in a container
Thank you all for your great work!

data.title: Vision Now Available in Llama.cpp
data.author: redman25
data.article_summary: llama.cpp 是由 ggml-org 开发的一个开源项目，旨在通过 C++ 实现对 LLaMA（Large Language Model Meta AI）的高效运行和优化。该项目特别关注在本地设备上（如个人电脑和移动设备）实现大语言模型的推理过程，而不依赖于云服务。通过使用量化技术，llama.cpp 能够显著减少模型运行时的计算资源需求，提高了运行速度和能效。该项目在 GitHub 上获得了广泛关注，拥有近 80,000 个星标和上万次代码分叉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：llama.cpp及其多模态模型（特别是Gemma系列）的性能、使用方法和应用场景

不同观点：
• **dust42** 和 **danielhanchen** 讨论了使用Gemma-3-4b模型时的性能表现。dust42提供了具体的性能数据（如每秒处理的token数量），并给出了详细的操作步骤，指出即使图片大小不同，整体处理时间也大约为15秒。danielhanchen补充了自己对模型速度的优化（如unsloth quants），并解释了如何利用Metal backend加速GPU处理。
• **ngxson** 提到了SmolVLM系列模型，强调其轻量化和快速响应的特性，特别适合实时视频监控等应用场景。
• **simonw** 提供了实际操作的文档链接，并分享了在macOS上的具体操作步骤，包括如何解决权限问题以及启动本地服务器。
• **banana_giraffe** 分享了使用Gemma-3 4b模型处理旅行照片的实际体验，指出其在OCR和图片内容识别方面的出色表现。
• **thenthenthen** 对llama.cpp近几个月的变化提出疑问，质疑其在图像描述功能上的新改进。
• **nico** 比较了llama.cpp和ollama等多模态模型在Mac上的表现，寻求社区的经验分享。
• **gitroom** 对Mac上加速模型运行的各种技巧表示赞赏，并提出这些改进是否会促使更多人开始在家玩转视觉处理。
• **dr_kiszonka** 提出了一个实际应用问题，询问是否有工具能够利用视觉处理来辅助UI开发，特别是与TS/React前端开发相关的工作流程。
• **a_e_k** 对llama.cpp的更新历史进行了简要回顾，特别提到了从多个CLI程序统一到一个单一CLI程序的过程，并对新加入的服务器支持表示赞赏。
• **gryfft** 认为llama.cpp的更新是阶梯式的进步，并预测边缘推理技术在个人助理等应用场景中的快速发展。
• **behnamoh** 质疑llama.cpp是否在去年就已经有了视觉支持。
• **mrs6969** 关心图像处理和图像生成之间的区别，并对当前的进展表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：部分用户（如thenthenthen和behnamoh）对llama.cpp新功能的实际改进提出质疑，认为其早前版本已经具备类似功能。
• 实际应用：banana_giraffe和dr_kiszonka分享了实际应用中的具体需求和场景，如旅行照片处理和前端开发中的视觉辅助工具。
• 性能优化：danielhanchen和gitroom讨论了如何通过各种技术手段（如Metal backend和多线程处理）来提升模型性能和运行速度。

data.title: Ash (Almquist Shell) Variants
data.author: thefilmore
data.article_summary: 本文概述了Ash（Almquist Shell）及其各种变体的历史和特性。Ash由Kenneth Almquist在1989年创建，作为传统System V Bourne shell的替代品，最早随BSD 4.3-Net/2发布。不同变体在命令替换、变量处理、错误处理、路径功能等方面存在差异。本文还列出了与SVR4 shell的比较，包括不支持命令行编辑、参数扩展和算术扩展等特性。此外，文章介绍了各个变体的发展历程，如386BSD、NetBSD、FreeBSD、BusyBox和Android变体，并提供了变体之间的家族树图示。最后，文章指出了一些早期变体的独特行为和未记录的特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：历史功能在不同环境下的表现和使用体验

不同观点：
• **barosl的观点**：该用户对历史课表示了积极的态度，并且对"dash"命令行具有历史功能感到新奇，尤其是提到该功能默认是禁用的。这表明该用户可能对命令行工具的细节了解相对较少，因此对新发现的功能表现出一定的惊喜。

补充讨论：
• 该评论还隐含了一个技术细节，即不同的命令行解释器（如dash）可能具有不同的默认配置，用户在使用过程中可能会遇到一些未主动开启或发现的功能。这可能会引发其他技术用户对如何启用、配置或利用这些功能的进一步讨论。

Ash (Almquist Shell) Variants
2006-02-14 .. 2021-02-13
(see
recent changes
)
After I had repeatedly wondered how all those "ash" variants
might be related, and had found hardly
any
information, I had a closer look at the variants I know.
Source is available for all variants, except for BSD/OS.
Thanks to
TUHS
for archiving the traditional BSDs and 386BSD,
to
Kirk McKusick
for his
CSRG archive
,
and to
Peter Seebach
for allowing me to learn all BSD/OS variants.
This page documents relationships.
And for the variants without changelogs (the traditional BSDs, 386BSD, BSD/OS and Minix)
this page aims at being a
complete
log concerning source code changes.
But for the other, later variants this was certainly not the goal and just a few,
arbitrarily chosen changes or bugfixes are listed.
Why no commented diffs? I won't manage to do that work. And if you're interested
on this level, then you are looking at the source already and these comments are a good start.

1.) Original release ('89) -
sh(1)
It was written by Kenneth Almquist as replacement to the
traditional "System V Release 4" Bourne shell
due to the license war between AT&T and Berkeley.
Berkeley distributed it first with "BSD 4.3-Net/2".
The source was
posted to comp.sources.unix, "A reimplementation of the System V shell"
, on 30-05-1989.
Shortly after, Kenneth published a
job control patch
to fix the problem that more than 4 jobs were not handled properly.
First, a few summaries for orientation, what it's about with these almquist shells.
Differences between the ash family and the SVR4 shell:
ash implements
"
$(...)
" command substitution
accepts
"
export VAR=value
"
echo
accepts option -e to interpret escape sequences (undocumented)
the file
DIFFERENCES
from the original distribution
lists most remaining differences to both the Berkeley shell
(a variant of the V7 shell) and the SVR4 shell.
A few differences are documented but not listed in this file, e.g.,
the built-ins "
bltin
" and "
setvar
"
only mentioned in the manual, but not explained:
built-ins
"catf"
,
"expr"
,
"line"
,
"nlecho"
a characteristic feature of almquist shells in general:
a PATH component flagged with a trailing "
%func
" is recognized
as a
directory containing function definitions
.
Read more about this.
another characteristic feature of almquist shells:
"local -"
makes
$-
local in functions (thanks to
Jilles Tjoelker
)
implements "
--
" as end of options for built-ins
"naturally", nothing from the list of
specific Bourne shell behaviour
is implemented.
Common to ash variants and the SVR4 shell only, in contrast to other bourne compatible shells:
"
notexistent_cmd 2>/dev/null
" doesn't redirect the error "not found"
(exception: dash since 0.4.17 and FreeBSD 9.0)
"
echo x > file*
" doesn't expand
file*
Details which are only found in early ash variants:
(only) the original release knew an
undocumented version variable:
SHELLVERS="ash 0.2"
Later variants can only be recognized and distinguished by characteristic features.
(A release "ash-0.2" of the later linux port is not related to this variable.)
like SVR4 sh:
no command line editing and history
(by intention)
like SVR4 sh:
no
#
and
%
form of parameter expansion
like SVR4 sh:
no arithmetic expansion
like SVR4 sh: no multi-digit parameter expansion like
${10}
like SVR4 sh: "
set --
" doesn't unset the parameter list
like SVR4 sh: traditional behaviour about
IFS vs. "$*"
by intention, there is
no backslash escaping in the back-tick form of
command substitution (
`...`
), side effect: this form cannot be nested
[changed in 4.4BSD]
undocumented: no "type" built-in
(probably accidentally) [fixed in NetBSD1.3,FreeBSD2.3]
read by default
behaves as if the POSIX
flag -r
is active
PS1 is "
@
"
with "
sh -c cmd arg0 arg1
",
$1
is set to
arg0
[fixed relatively late: all traditional BSDs, and early Free-/NetBSDs and early Minix
behave as well]
bug: "
VAR=set eval 'echo $VAR'
" gives no output
,
that is, you can't call
eval
with local variables
"
for i do
" not accepted
(but "
for i; do
" or "
for i<newline>do
")
flag
-v
not implemented
reads SHINIT at start
(except if a login shell or called with "sh file")
"
trap
" doesn't accept symbol

data.title: Stratolaunch Successfully Completes Reusable Hypersonic Flight and Recovery
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 2025年5月，Stratolaunch公司宣布其Talon-A2（TA-2）全自动高超音速飞行器在2025年3月成功完成第二次可重复使用高超音速飞行与回收任务。此次飞行速度再次超过5马赫，验证了飞行器的可重复使用性。首次飞行于2024年12月完成，同样达到了高超音速。两次飞行收集的数据将用于提升Talon-A系列飞行器的性能。此次成功标志着美国自1968年X-15项目结束后，重新实现可重复使用高超音速飞行测试。这些成就对国防和技术测试具有重要意义，并为未来的高超音速飞行测试奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Stratolaunch及其相关技术的性质和实用性

不同观点：
• imcritic的评论主要是技术性问题，表明他无法访问stratolaunch.com网站，并寻求解决建议。这并不是对技术本身的评价，而是对访问问题的关注。

• ChuckMcM认为Stratolaunch更像是一个功能或技术展示，而非一个完整的产品。他将Stratolaunch比作洛克希德或波音的一个部门项目，暗示这可能只是一个较大系统中的一个组件，而不是具有独立市场价值的产品。

• superkuh则深入分析了Stratolaunch涉及的技术，特别是对“高超音速飞行器”和“简单锥形火箭”进行了区分。superkuh指出，Stratolaunch及其类似的“高超音速”项目在实际能力上与弹道导弹并无太大区别，只是在轨迹上有所不同。他还质疑这些项目的实际用途，认为它们可能是为了留住航空航天人才或使弹道导弹的使用正常化。

补充讨论：
• superkuh进一步指出，虽然高超音速飞行器的研发具有科学价值，特别是在避免冲击波影响方面，但Stratolaunch本身并未实现这些真正的技术突破。

• 争议的焦点在于Stratolaunch是否真正代表了高超音速技术的前沿，还是仅仅是一个“纸老虎”项目，用于维持技术人才和资源的运作。

• ChuckMcM和superkuh的观点都对Stratolaunch的实际市场或技术价值持怀疑态度，但ChuckMcM更关注其作为产品的定位，而superkuh则深入探讨了其技术实质和潜在的政治用途。

通过这些评论，可以看出对Stratolaunch的评价存在分歧，主要围绕其技术实质和市场定位展开讨论。

May 5, 2025
Stratolaunch Successfully Completes Reusable Hypersonic Flight and Recovery with Talon-A2 Vehicle
Source: Stratolaunch
MOJAVE, CA â May 05, 2025 â
Stratolaunch is pleased to announce the successful completion of its second hypersonic flight and recovery with the Talon-A2 (TA-2) fully autonomous vehicle in March 2025. We are also pleased to share that this significant accomplishment followed the successful first hypersonic flight of Talon-A2 in December 2024 confirming the demonstrated reusability of the vehicle. The vehicle surpassed Mach 5 during its trajectory for the second time, exceeding the previous speed record set with the December flight.
With the data collected from this second flight, we are able to apply lessons learned to enhance the strength and performance of the Talon-A vehicles. While the team needs to complete its data review of flight two, the first flight review confirmed the robustness of the Talon-A design while demonstrating the ability to meet the full range of performance capabilities desired by our customers. Weâve now demonstrated hypersonic speed, added the complexity of a full runway landing with prompt payload recovery, and proven reusability. Both flights were great achievements for our country, our company, and our partners.
Dr. Zachary Krevor
President and CEO of Stratolaunch
Credit: Stratolaunch / Julian Guerra
Supporting the United Statesâ defense initiatives, Stratolaunch is focused on expanding its hypersonic flight testing and ensuring the long-term sustainability of reusable hypersonic testbeds. These completed flights demonstrate the United Statesâ return to reusable hypersonic flight test since the X-15 program ended in 1968.Â
Â
âI am in awe of what this team has achieved. Weâve executed four incredible Talon-A flights, completed twenty-four Roc flights to date, flew two new supersonic and hypersonic airplanes in a single year, and we are firmly on the path to making hypersonic flight test services a reality,â Krevor said.Â Â
Credit: Stratolaunch / Brandon Lim
Stratolaunch performed the flights for the Test Resource Management Center (TRMC) Multi-Service Advanced Capability Hypersonic Test Bed (MACH-TB) program under a partnership with Leidos. The MACH-TB program is intended to increase the speed of testing for all commercially available hypersonic systems. This was the second Stratolaunch flight completed on behalf of the program.Â
These flights were a huge success for our program and for the nation. The data collected from the experiments flown on the initial Talon-A flight has now been analyzed and the results are extremely positive. The opportunity for technology testing at a high rate is highly valuable as we push the pace of hypersonic testing.  The MACH-TB program is pleased with the multiple flight successes while looking forward to future flight tests with Stratolaunch.
Scott Wilson
Program Manager of MACH-TB
âDemonstrating the reuse of fully recoverable hypersonic test vehicles is an important milestone for MACH-TB," stated George Rumford, Director of the Department of Defense Test Resource Management Center. "Lessons learned from this test campaign will help us reduce vehicle turnaround time from months down to weeks.âÂ

data.title: Show HN: A backend agnostic Ruby framework for building reactive desktop apps
data.author: zero-st4rs
data.article_summary: Hokusai 是一个与后端无关的 Ruby 框架，用于构建响应式桌面应用程序。它支持 Windows，并依赖于不同的图形库（如 Raylib 或 SDL2）来运行应用程序。该项目使用 xmake 作为构建工具，包含 tree-sitter 语法解析模板和 md4c 解析 markdown。主要功能包括通过编写 Ruby 代码和模板创建 GUI 应用，如一个简单的计数器示例。Hokusai 基于 MIT 许可证发布，要求使用 Ruby 运行应用，并通过 xmake 编译相关依赖和代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个新项目的许可证兼容性、功能、实际应用以及技术选择。

不同观点：
• [许可证问题] viraptor指出该项目的许可证信息不明确，未列在OSI（开放源代码促进会）上，因此在使用和发布时存在法律风险，需要阅读大量法律文件才能确定其兼容性。
• [积极反馈] omneity和xfalcox对项目表示赞赏，认为它让人联想到"shoes.rb"项目，并且可以用于创建有用的组件（widgets）。
• [许可证疑问] jenadine首次听闻"copyfarleft license"，并质疑这种许可证对库的实际影响。
• [技术可行性] az09mugen对项目选择Raylib或SDL2表示赞赏，并询问是否可以添加Android作为目标平台，给出了Raylib编译到Android的参考链接。
• [部署问题] zem关注部署问题，询问该项目是否可以用于发布应用程序，使得终端用户无需了解Hokusai或Ruby。
• [示例需求] iraliaf对项目表示感谢，并询问是否有示例网站，因为未能找到参考。
• [技术比较] whalesalad将该项目与RubyMotion进行比较，询问两者的优劣。
• [技术选择] dismalaf对使用xmake而不是rake表示好奇，询问原因。
• [UI开发实践] samiv质疑当前通过代码编写UI的实际开发实践，提出自己使用Qt Designer通过拖放生成UI代码的经验，认为这种方法更快更简单。

补充讨论：
• 许可证的模糊性是讨论中的一个主要争议点，影响到项目的使用和发布。
• 关于技术实现，有人关注跨平台支持（如Android），有人则关注与类似工具（如RubyMotion、Qt Designer）的比较。
• 项目的实际应用和部署问题也被多次提及，显示出社区对项目实用性的关注。
• 不同的技术选择（如xmake vs. rake）引发了对开发流程效率的讨论。
• 最后，UI开发实践的讨论揭示了不同开发者在UI设计中的偏好和工具选择的多样性。

43938309.article_summary: Hokusai 是一个与后端无关的 Ruby 框架，用于构建响应式桌面应用程序。它支持 Windows，并依赖于不同的图形库（如 Raylib 或 SDL2）来运行应用程序。该项目使用 xmake 作为构建工具，包含 tree-sitter 语法解析模板和 md4c 解析 markdown。主要功能包括通过编写 Ruby 代码和模板创建 GUI 应用，如一个简单的计数器示例。Hokusai 基于 MIT 许可证发布，要求使用 Ruby 运行应用，并通过 xmake 编译相关依赖和代码。

data.title: LegoGPT: Generating Physically Stable and Buildable Lego
data.author: nkko
data.article_summary: LegoGPT是一种能够根据文本描述生成物理稳定且可拼搭乐高结构的模型。该模型使用大规模、物理稳定的乐高设计数据集（StableText2Lego）进行训练，数据集包含超过47,000个乐高结构及其详细描述。通过自回归大型语言模型，LegoGPT可以逐块预测生成乐高设计，并在生成过程中进行有效性检查和物理回滚，以确保结构的稳定性。实验表明，LegoGPT生成的设计稳定、多样且美观，与输入文本高度一致。此外，模型还支持通过机械臂自动组装乐高结构，并能够生成带颜色和纹理的设计。该研究还公开了数据集、代码和模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成乐高设计的稳定性、实用性、法律问题以及用户体验。

不同观点：
• **Haberman**：认为AI在特定约束下生成和优化设计（如交通灯或乐高结构）是非常有趣且有潜力的应用。强调通过物理法则和组装约束来筛选不可行的设计，并指出设计问题空间和约束是关键。

• **Sschueller**：担心使用“LEGO”一词可能引发法律问题，建议避免使用该词以规避乐高公司的律师函风险。

• **Stevage**：对当前AI生成结果的质量提出质疑，认为手动设计的算法可能会比AI生成的结果更好，尤其是在使用少量砖块时，AI生成的设计看起来不像预期。

• **Jader201**：指出网页在iPhone上的技术问题，当滚动到GIF部分时会自动加载，导致导航困难。

• **RaSoJo**：认为乐高搭建的乐趣在于手工操作，自动化并非必要。反而希望在搭建后进行自动化整理、分类和存储砖块，解决现实中的实际问题。

• **Yathaid**：对项目表示赞赏，分享了相关的数据集和代码资源，并对展示的GIF动画表示兴趣。

• **Psiops**：指出AI生成的设计在自动组装时可能存在问题，例如悬浮砖块的放置顺序会导致机器人组装困难。

• **Gilgoomesh**：以幽默的方式评论机器人组装乐高的低效，将其比喻为机器人养老院。

• **Kilimounjaro**：认为该项目只是将3D模型转换为体素和砖块，没有太大创新。建议举办Kaggle竞赛以探索更好的算法来自动生成有趣的乐高设计。

• **Carstenhag**：关注乐高公司的商标问题，提醒项目作者注意乐高公司的严格商标保护政策。

• **Dwighttk**：抱怨文章中的视频自动全屏播放，导致阅读体验不佳。

• **W0lfEagle**：建议将该技术应用于橱柜设计，并给出具体的材料和设计约束，认为这种应用更有实际价值。

• **9dev**：以个人经历回应，表示曾梦想成为专业乐高搭建者，感叹科技发展使得这一职业梦想变得可能。

• **Soared**：对高背椅的GIF示例进行分析，指出AI设计中存在的不合理砖块使用问题，认为反向构建会更稳定，并对整体概念表示肯定。

补充讨论：
- 项目中的法律风险，尤其是乐高公司可能的商标和知识产权问题。
- 用户体验问题，包括网页自动加载GIF和视频播放对阅读体验的影响。
- 对AI生成设计结果的质量和实用性的质疑，以及手动算法可能的优势。
- 对未来应用场景的建议，如橱柜设计和乐高搭建后的自动化整理。
- 对项目技术细节的深入探讨，如砖块选择和设计顺序对稳定性的影响。

43933891.article_content:
LegoGPT: Generating Physically Stable and Buildable LEGO® Designs from Text
Ava Pun
*
Kangle Deng
*
Ruixuan Liu
*
Deva Ramanan
Changliu Liu
Jun-Yan Zhu
Carnegie Mellon University
* denotes equal contribution
arXiv
Code
Demo
Overview
LegoGPT
generates a LEGO structure from a user-provided text prompt in an end-to-end manner. Notably, our generated LEGO structure is physically stable and buildable.
Abstract
We introduce
LegoGPT
, the first approach for generating physically stable LEGO brick models from text prompts. To achieve this, we construct a large-scale, physically stable dataset of LEGO designs, along with their associated captions, and train an autoregressive large language model to predict the next brick to add via next-token prediction. To improve the stability of the resulting designs, we employ an efficient validity check and physics-aware rollback during autoregressive inference, which prunes infeasible token predictions using physics laws and assembly constraints. Our experiments show that
LegoGPT
produces stable, diverse, and aesthetically pleasing LEGO designs that align closely with the input text prompts. We also develop a text-based LEGO texturing method to generate colored and textured designs. We show that our designs can be assembled manually by humans and automatically by robotic arms. We also release our new dataset,
StableText2Lego
, containing over 47,000 LEGO structures of over 28,000 unique 3D objects accompanied by detailed captions, along with our code and models.
StableText2Lego Dataset
(a) From a ShapeNetCore mesh, we generate a LEGO design by voxelizing it onto a \(20\times 20 \times 20\) grid and applying legolization to determine the brick layout. (b) We augment each shape with multiple structural variations by randomizing the brick layout while preserving the overall shape. (c) Stability analysis is performed on each variation to filter out physically unstable designs. (d) To obtain the corresponding captions for each shape, we render the LEGO design from 24 different viewpoints and use GPT-4o to generate detailed geometric descriptions. (e) Data samples from 5 categories in our
StableText2Lego
dataset.
LegoGPT Pipeline
(a) Our system tokenizes a LEGO design into a sequence of text tokens,  ordered in a raster-scan manner from bottom to top. (b) We create an instruction dataset pairing brick sequences with descriptions to fine-tune LLaMA-3.2-Instruct-1B. (c) At inference time,
LegoGPT
generates LEGO designs incrementally by predicting one brick at a time given a text prompt. For each generated brick, we perform validity checks to ensure it is well-formatted, exists in our brick library, and does not collide with existing bricks. After completing the design, we verify its physical stability. If the structure is unstable, we roll back to the stable state by removing all the unstable bricks and their subsequent ones and resume generation from that point.

data.title: The most valuable commodity in the world is friction
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：摩擦与数字世界中的价值创造、效率与适应

不同观点：
• **muzani** 认为，"摩擦债务"（friction debt）是数字产品中的一种策略，比如Freemium模式，用户现在无摩擦地免费使用产品，但将来通过付费去除摩擦，最终付出的成本比一次性购买更高。这个观点强调了商业模式中的延迟摩擦成本。
• **jfengel** 基本同意该观点，但认为“摩擦”这个术语不恰当，摩擦并不是商品或有价值的东西，而是创造价值的过程。他将其比作艺术来自对某种限制的斗争，限制本身可能是不合理的，但正因为这种限制，结果才有了意义。
• **fellowniusmonk** 提出，互联网的本质是低摩擦和高可观察性，但这也导致了高摩擦、低可观察性的现实问题被忽视。数字平台为了吸引用户参与，引导人们远离现实世界和真实的人际关系，最终可能导致用数字替代现实。
• **zkmon** 认为，"摩擦"只是现实世界的一部分，它会一直存在。数字世界和虚拟技术只是短暂的潮流，最终现实会恢复正常。人类对现实世界的影响很小，文化和新思想的兴起和衰落是自然的适应过程。
• **apples_oranges** 则从另一个角度看待数字世界，认为它几乎全是摩擦，因为无用的信息充斥着我们的大脑，使我们无法正常运作。离线状态反而是一种解脱。

补充讨论：
• **eviks** 对"无摩擦"的数字天堂提出质疑，认为像Amazon的一键下单实际上是将摩擦转嫁给了仓库工人和送货司机。Meta的社交界面也无法完全匹配用户的需求，这怎么能算无摩擦？
• **Animats** 提到了一些相关的文章和采访，认为这些内容比关于"摩擦"的文章更有价值。
• **cadamsdotcom** 指出，美国文化崇尚发明和新事物，但对老旧基础设施的维护却常常被忽视。尽管如此，美国仍在许多方面继续运行良好。
• **raffael_de** 质疑作者没有明确定义"摩擦"的具体含义，认为文章是基于过度延伸的类比。
• **dgan** 提到，最近有很多Substack投稿，并抱怨在Android设备上无法关闭cookie横幅，因此没有阅读。
• **3abiton** 对系统从设计为弹性转向优化效率时的失败表示关注，并询问去除摩擦是否有助于透明度的确保。
• **ranprieur** 强调，系统在优化效率时会失去弹性并最终崩溃。
• **teddy-smith** 认为，在美国，钱是解决问题的主要方式，因此生活中的摩擦与你的金钱成反比。

争议焦点：
• 对"摩擦"这一术语的理解和定义存在争议。一些人认为摩擦是创造价值的过程，而不是需要消除的障碍。
• 数字世界是否真正减少了摩擦，还是只是将摩擦转嫁到了其他方面或人身上，也存在不同看法。

主要讨论点：摩擦与数字世界中的价值创造、效率与适应

不同观点：
• **muzani** 认为，"摩擦债务"（friction debt）是数字产品中的一种策略，比如Freemium模式，用户现在无摩擦地免费使用产品，但将来通过付费去除摩擦，最终付出的成本比一次性购买更高。这个观点强调了商业模式中的延迟摩擦成本。
• **jfengel** 基本同意该观点，但认为“摩擦”这个术语不恰当，摩擦并不是商品或有价值的东西，而是创造价值的过程。他将其比作艺术来自对某种限制的斗争，限制本身可能是不合理的，但正因为这种限制，结果才有了意义。
• **fellowniusmonk** 提出，互联网的本质是低摩擦和高可观察性，但这也导致了高摩擦、低可观察性的现实问题被忽视。数字平台为了吸引用户参与，引导人们远离现实世界和真实的人际关系，最终可能导致用数字替代现实。
• **zkmon** 认为，"摩擦"只是现实世界的一部分，它会一直存在。数字世界和虚拟技术只是短暂的潮流，最终现实会恢复正常。人类对现实世界的影响很小，文化和新思想的兴起和衰落是自然的适应过程。
• **apples_oranges** 则从另一个角度看待数字世界，认为它几乎全是摩擦，因为无用的信息充斥着我们的大脑，使我们无法正常运作。离线状态反而是一种解脱。

补充讨论：
• **eviks** 对"无摩擦"的数字天堂提出质疑，认为像Amazon的一键下单实际上是将摩擦转嫁给了仓库工人和送货司机。Meta的社交界面也无法完全匹配用户的需求，这怎么能算无摩擦？
• **Animats** 提到了一些相关的文章和采访，认为这些内容比关于"摩擦"的文章更有价值。
• **cadamsdotcom** 指出，美国文化崇尚发明和新事物，但对老旧基础设施的维护却常常被忽视。尽管如此，美国仍在许多方面继续运行良好。
• **raffael_de** 质疑作者没有明确定义"摩擦"的具体含义，认为文章是基于过度延伸的类比。
• **dgan** 提到，最近有很多Substack投稿，并抱怨在Android设备上无法关闭cookie横幅，因此没有阅读。
• **3abiton** 对系统从设计为弹性转向优化效率时的失败表示关注，并询问去除摩擦是否有助于透明度的确保。
• **ranprieur** 强调，系统在优化效率时会失去弹性并最终崩溃。
• **teddy-smith** 认为，在美国，钱是解决问题的主要方式，因此生活中的摩擦与你的金钱成反比。

争议焦点：
• 对"摩擦"这一术语的理解和定义存在争议。一些人认为摩擦是创造价值的过程，而不是需要消除的障碍。
• 数字世界是否真正减少了摩擦，还是只是将摩擦转嫁到了其他方面或人身上，也存在不同看法。

News
|
May 6, 2025
Title of Work Deciphered In Sealed Herculaneum Scroll Via Digital Unwrapping
2025 Vesuvius Challenge
The scroll's title
The
Bodleian Libraries
and the Vesuvius Challenge have announced that for the first time researchers have found the title and author inside of a
sealed scroll from Herculaneum
.
Using ‘virtual unwrapping’, the scroll PHerc. 172 which is housed at the Bodleian Libraries at the University of Oxford has been identified as
On Vices
by the Greek philosopher Philodemus. The ethical treatise, known in full as
On Vices and Their Opposite Virtues and In Whom They Are and About What
, provides guidance for cultivating a virtuous life. In recognition of this achievement, researchers have been awarded the Vesuvius Challenge First Title Prize which includes prize money of $60,000.
Following the scanning of the scroll in July 2024 at the Diamond Light Source in Harwell, the Vesuvius Challenge released the data publicly, inviting researchers worldwide to contribute to deciphering the text. While the first images of the inside of the scroll were published in February 2025, the discovery of the title page within the innermost part of the scroll required considerable analysis before it could be accurately read and interpreted by papyrologists.
This was independently achieved by two parties at roughly the same time, by Sean Johnson from the Vesuvius Challenge, and contestant research team Marcel Roth and Micha Nowak from the University of Würzburg. The pair, whose submission further refined the degree of legibility, have been awarded the first Vesuvius Challenge First Title Prize, in recognition of their success in revealing the title.
Both images were independently reviewed by the Vesuvius Challenge papyrological team, led by Federica Nicolardi. The  simultaneous reproduction of the title image from multiple sources, along with independent scholarly review, provides a high degree of confidence in the reading.
Philodemus (c. 110–c 30 BCE) was an Epicurean philosopher and poet from Gadara whose ethical teachings emphasise the pursuit of pleasure as central to a good life. He argued against rigid logic and formal rhetoric, believing that philosophy should serve practical human happiness rather than abstract intellectual debate. As the author whose works make up the majority of the library in the Villa of Papyri at Herculaneum, it is unsurprising that he was the author of this work too.
While the scroll’s author and title are now clear, where the text sits within the
On Vices
series, known by scholars to be at least 10 books long, is still open to interpretation. The book number in the title image is plausibly read as an alpha, indicating that this scroll is Book 1. However, the reading  is still uncertain, and other possibilities (e.g. delta, Book 4), while less likely, cannot be completely ruled out. If it is indeed Book 1, this raises further questions since it has generally been understood that the first book of the
On Vices
was
On Flattery
, but the text of PHerc. 172 does not correspond with this.
“This is a very exciting development," said Michael McOsker, a esearcher in Papyrology at UCL who is a member of the Vesuvius Challenge Papyrology Team and one of the editors of this scroll based at the University of Oxford. "Other books from the
On Vices and their Opposite Virtues
are known from the papyri that were physically unrolled. Best known are
On Property Management,
book 9 and presumably the opposite virtue to greed, and
On Arrogance,
book 10, presumably the opposite vice to having a correct evaluation of yourself, but there are others too. This will be a great opportunity to learn more about Philodemus’ ethical views and to get a better view of the
On Vices
as a whole, especially if it turns out to be the first book. As a technical matter, it’s great that progress continues apace and we’ll soon be able to read these rolls in their entireties.”
Richard Ovenden
, Bodley’s Librarian & Helen Hamlyn Director of the University Libraries, said: “Finding the full title of a work inside a scroll that has been unread for two millennia is an astonishing achievement, and illustrates the huge potential for AI to transform arts and humanities scholarship, our understanding of the past, and breathes new life into ancient artefacts.”
The Vesuvius Challenge, the global initiative that was launched in 2023 to discover the contents of the Herculaneum Scrolls without any physical intervention to the scrolls themselves, continues to encourage contributions from researchers across the world. Created by Dr Brent Seales at the University of Kentucky, Nat Friedman, and Daniel Gross, the initiative has rewarded teams across the world for their discoveries, including first ink detection and various open-source software
contributions.

data.title: Show HN: GlassFlow – OSS streaming dedup and joins from Kafka to ClickHouse
data.author: super_ar
data.article_summary: GlassFlow for ClickHouse Streaming ETL 是一个实时流处理工具，旨在简化 Kafka 到 ClickHouse 的数据管道构建与管理。其主要功能包括实时数据去重和时间序列连接，支持配置时间窗口（最长7天）和去重/连接键。它内置 Kafka 连接器，通过 NATS-Kafka Bridge 自动提取数据，并优化了 ClickHouse 数据写入。该工具提供直观的web界面，支持Docker部署和本地开发，具备高吞吐量处理能力和简化的管道配置流程，适合数据工程师使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GlassFlow项目与ClickHouse中ReplacingMergeTree (RMT) 的比较，以及对去重机制的实现细节和适用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• hodgesrm：认为RMT虽然需要在读取时付出一定代价，并且需要针对性能优化设计模式，但其去重行为相对容易理解。相比之下，GlassFlow的去重机制可能需要更多的细节来证明其优势。
• caust1c：对去重系统的可扩展性表示怀疑，指出需要考虑网络延迟、数据源流的 partitioning/sharding、以及处理写入目标失败等问题。他提到曾维护过类似的去重管道，对细节不足的系统持谨慎态度。
• ram_rar：提出RMT可以有效解决去重问题，并通过查询时过滤进一步优化，质疑GlassFlow的必要性。
• YZF：关注如何避免ClickHouse中的重复行，提出插入失败和去重服务器崩溃等场景下的数据一致性问题。
• maxboone：对NATS直接流配置表示关注，询问通过NATS桥接Kafka的配置工作量。
• saisrirampur：询问去重是否仅针对整行重复，还是可以处理部分列冲突，并指出若在数据摄入ClickHouse前去重，可能仅能处理前者。
• darkbatman：关注项目的负载测试结果，希望了解其在高规模下的表现。
• the_arun：询问项目为何仅限于ClickHouse和Kafka，是否能通用化，并关注默认负载测试情况。
• brap：赞赏设计，关心是内部开发还是外包。
• oulipo：对去重的具体场景表示疑惑，询问Kafka或ClickHouse为何不能通过主键自行去重，并描述IoT设备数据批量摄入的用例。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：GlassFlow去重机制的必要性及其相对于RMT的优势。
• 关注点：去重系统的可扩展性、失败场景下的数据一致性、系统负载测试结果、以及通用性。
• 实用场景：包括Kafka重复行发送、IoT设备数据批量摄入等。

GlassFlow for ClickHouse Streaming ETL
GlassFlow for ClickHouse Streaming ETL is a real-time stream processor designed to simplify data pipeline creation and management between Kafka and ClickHouse. It provides a powerful, user-friendly interface for building and managing real-time data pipelines with built-in support for deduplication and temporal joins.
Built specifically for data engineers, GlassFlow handles late-arriving events, ensures exactly-once correctness, and scales with high-throughput data. It delivers accurate, low-latency results from streaming data without compromising simplicity or performance. The tool's intuitive web interface makes it easy to configure and monitor pipelines, while its robust architecture ensures reliable data processing.
Key Features
Streaming Deduplication
:
Real-time deduplication of Kafka streams before ingestion into ClickHouse
Configurable time windows up to 7 days for deduplication
Simple configuration of deduplication keys and time windows
One-click setup for deduplicated data pipelines
Prevents duplicate data from reaching ClickHouse
Temporal Stream Joins
:
Join two Kafka streams in real-time
Configurable time windows up to 7 days for stream joins
Configure join keys and time windows through the UI
Simplified join setup process
Produce joined streams ready for ClickHouse ingestion
Built-in Kafka Connector
:
Powered by
NATS-Kafka Bridge
Automatic data extraction from Kafka topics
Seamless integration with Kafka clusters
No manual data pulling required
Supports multiple Kafka topics and partitions
Native support for JSON data types
Optimized ClickHouse Sink
:
Native ClickHouse connection for maximum performance
Configurable batch sizes for efficient data ingestion
Adjustable wait times for optimal throughput
Built-in retry mechanisms
Automatic schema detection and management
Full support for JSON data types in ClickHouse
User-Friendly Interface
: Web-based UI for pipeline configuration and management
Local Development
: Includes demo setup with local Kafka and ClickHouse instances
Docker Support
: Easy deployment using Docker and docker-compose
Self-Hosted
: Open-source solution that can be self-hosted in your infrastructure

Git

cd
clickhouse-etl

http://localhost:8080
to configure your pipeline:

:

Configure ClickHouse sink connection parameters

:

Define deduplication key and time window
For joins: specify join keys and time window for each stream
Configure ClickHouse table settings

:

Creating a Pipeline

http://localhost:8080

43953722.article_summary: GlassFlow for ClickHouse Streaming ETL 是一个实时流处理工具，旨在简化 Kafka 到 ClickHouse 的数据管道构建与管理。其主要功能包括实时数据去重和时间序列连接，支持配置时间窗口（最长7天）和去重/连接键。它内置 Kafka 连接器，通过 NATS-Kafka Bridge 自动提取数据，并优化了 ClickHouse 数据写入。该工具提供直观的web界面，支持Docker部署和本地开发，具备高吞吐量处理能力和简化的管道配置流程，适合数据工程师使用。
43953722.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GlassFlow项目与ClickHouse中ReplacingMergeTree (RMT) 的比较，以及对去重机制的实现细节和适用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• hodgesrm：认为RMT虽然需要在读取时付出一定代价，并且需要针对性能优化设计模式，但其去重行为相对容易理解。相比之下，GlassFlow的去重机制可能需要更多的细节来证明其优势。
• caust1c：对去重系统的可扩展性表示怀疑，指出需要考虑网络延迟、数据源流的 partitioning/sharding、以及处理写入目标失败等问题。他提到曾维护过类似的去重管道，对细节不足的系统持谨慎态度。
• ram_rar：提出RMT可以有效解决去重问题，并通过查询时过滤进一步优化，质疑GlassFlow的必要性。
• YZF：关注如何避免ClickHouse中的重复行，提出插入失败和去重服务器崩溃等场景下的数据一致性问题。
• maxboone：对NATS直接流配置表示关注，询问通过NATS桥接Kafka的配置工作量。
• saisrirampur：询问去重是否仅针对整行重复，还是可以处理部分列冲突，并指出若在数据摄入ClickHouse前去重，可能仅能处理前者。
• darkbatman：关注项目的负载测试结果，希望了解其在高规模下的表现。
• the_arun：询问项目为何仅限于ClickHouse和Kafka，是否能通用化，并关注默认负载测试情况。
• brap：赞赏设计，关心是内部开发还是外包。
• oulipo：对去重的具体场景表示疑惑，询问Kafka或ClickHouse为何不能通过主键自行去重，并描述IoT设备数据批量摄入的用例。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：GlassFlow去重机制的必要性及其相对于RMT的优势。
• 关注点：去重系统的可扩展性、失败场景下的数据一致性、系统负载测试结果、以及通用性。
• 实用场景：包括Kafka重复行发送、IoT设备数据批量摄入等。

data.title: In 2025, venture capital can't pretend everything is fine any more
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: 2025年第一季度风险投资监测报告显示，风险投资行业陷入困境，唯一被寄予厚望的是人工智能（AI）领域，尤其是OpenAI。由于特朗普的关税政策和利率上升，风险资本面临系统性问题，投资和募资活动受阻。过去十年，低利率环境促使大量资金涌入初创企业，导致许多不靠谱的创业公司获得融资，如WeWork的失败。随着利率回升，资金转向更安全的投资渠道，如国债，风险投资失去吸引力。目前，AI成为投资人追求高回报的最后一搏，但这种泡沫前景不明。整体来看，除AI外，其他领域几乎陷入停滞，行业亟待解决深层问题，却缺乏有效方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风险投资（VC）和人工智能（AI）领域的现状及未来发展

不同观点：
• A_D_E_P_T认为，风投领域除了AI以外几乎停滞不前，而AI领域又几乎被OpenAI主导。OpenAI的激进投资策略被视为一种高风险的豪赌，尽管AI技术在过去几年中取得了显著进展，但目前的发展似乎遇到了瓶颈，超级智能是否能实现仍不确定。
• drdrek指出，风投对AI的追逐是“害怕错过”（FOMO）心理的体现。很多公司只是为了吸引资本而贴上AI标签，这可能夸大了AI在风投中的实际占比。未来十年，风投热点会转向其他 buzzword。
• TrapLord_Rhodo认为，VC模式正在崩溃，越来越多成功的企业通过自筹资金和社区支持发展，而非依赖VC。创始人通过个人品牌和多渠道推广产品，降低了对外部投资的需求。
• oli5679则持乐观态度，指出高增长公司仍有巨大潜力，并以Google的成长为例，强调技术趋势带来的巨大收益。
• enahs-sf关注VC如何通过管理费获利，指出即使基金失败，VC仍可通过管理费获得可观收入，这是VC模式中的“下限保护”。
• jparishy认为，当前是新模型和创业范式出现的绝佳时机，但VC模式过于单一，且在风险承受能力上发生了变化。虽然资金充裕，但并未有效利用。
• 999900000999以自嘲方式表达对AI创业的无奈，提到AI应用的普遍性和竞争激烈。
• sonicgear1对AI的扩张持负面态度，期待其“衰落”。
• culebron21观察到AI宣传者从激进 hype 转向更谨慎的态度，指出这些“专家”曾在多个技术潮流中追逐短期利益。
• jay-barronville提到，近年来创始人对待风投的态度发生了变化，更多人将其视为一次性机会，而非持续融资过程，这可能影响VC的未来运作方式。
• asdev认为，AI投资的高预期价值迫使投资者继续下注。
• vessenes反驳A_D_E_P_T的观点，认为当前市场存在无限的创新机会，并以一个快速盈利的公司为例，强调早期进入者可能成为未来的财富巨头。
• jmclnx建议投资于实际产品，而非短期投机。
• Beltiras认为现状并无变化，一切如常。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI和VC的未来发展方向。一方认为AI投资风险高且进展缓慢，另一方则认为AI及技术创新仍有巨大潜力。
• 风投模式的可持续性和变化也是讨论重点，包括VC如何通过管理费获利及创始人对风投的态度转变。
• 个人对AI扩张的看法从乐观到悲观不一，反映出对技术潮流的不同立场。

43953884.article_content:
Venture capital is screwed. A bubble in AI is their last hope, and they’re betting everything on Sam Altman. It’s heartwarming.
Today, we have the Pitchbook-NVCA Venture Monitor for Q1 2025. This is the National Venture Capital Association telling its members how things are going. It’s the view of VC from the inside. The front cover picture is the light at the end of the tunnel — and it’s an oncoming streetcar. [
NVCA
;
NVCA
, PDF
]
We covered the
Q3 2024 report
last year. That one tried very hard to present bad news as okay news. The new report can’t even do that.
Here is the state of venture capital in early 2025:
Venture capital is moribund except AI.
AI is moribund except OpenAI.
OpenAI is a weird scam that wants to burn money so fast it summons AI God.
Nobody can cash out.
The report mostly blames venture’s woes on President Trump and his tariffs — but venture capital’s problems are systemic and you could see them coming since the zero-interest-rate era.
And they have
no idea
how to fix this. None at all. The report’s
only
plan for the future is to cross their fingers and hope.
Trump’s tariffs have trashed everything
The Trump economic disaster is the most important material fact for the venture capital sphere. The report goes on and on about the tariffs.
Here’s the first paragraph of the report:
With uncertainty dominating US financial markets throughout the first quarter, our prior expectation that 2025 would see a resurgence in venture capital (VC) liquidity and dealmaking has been dimmed. Should the latest iteration of tariffs stand, we expect significant pressure on fundraising and dealmaking in the near term as investors sit on the sidelines and wait for signs of market stabilization.
That is: nobody is doing deals because business can’t make plans past lunchtime.
The report somehow fails to mention the bit where the Silicon Valley VC and executive crowd worked their backsides off to elect Trump and several of them sat in the front row at his inauguration. Then they were actually surprised when the leopard ate their faces too.
The end of zero interest
VC is hilariously unable to cope with not being in a zero-interest-rate environment.
In 2008, the global financial crisis hit. Central banks use interest rates as the brakes on an economy, so they took the brakes off to make sure money kept flowing around. Interest rates went below 1%. And interest stayed near zero for over a decade. [
St Louis Fed
]
But zero interest meant that if you
had
to get returns — say, you’re a pension fund — then there weren’t a lot of places to invest. Venture capital was one place you could put money and get returns.
This meant a flood of money into startups, and that meant all sorts of ridiculous startups got funding. Businesses that lost money on every transaction. SoftBank was setting money on fire as fast as possible, ending in the disaster of WeWork.
Borrowing money was almost free as well. Why not load up on debt?
But then inflation came along, and the Fed put interest rates back up — and suddenly there was less money. Why put money into venture capital when you could get back 5% just buying Treasury bills?
Venture capitalists were around before 2008 — including a lot of the current guys! — but it’s like they completely forgot how to do anything without free money. The party’s over, and now it’s time for the hangover.
So we get hyped up tech bubbles praying for lottery-level returns — because ordinary business returns from, say, making a thing and selling it don’t cut it. Our present hype-fueled AI bubble is a complete worked example.
Everything is OpenAI
This year, the investors are all-in on AI. Crypto’s still dead, quantum isn’t taking off — AI’s the last game in the casino. [
TechCrunch
]
There’s lots of graphs in this report showing healthy dollar amounts. These are mostly the
“$40 billion” OpenAI deal led by Softbank
, and then the other AI startup deals. Almost all the graphs and statistics in this report are lies based on the one huge OpenAI outlier.
Andreessen Horowitz is right now
raising a fresh $20 billion investment fund
to try to keep the AI bubble going.
VCs still believe the marketing brochure version of AI, because they don’t actually know anything about technology:
Just as “internet” evolved from buzzword to business backbone, AI is following the same playbook.
No it isn’t! A completely different thing taking off and working says nothing about whether your personal favourite thing will take off and work! Stop saying dumb things!
Pitchbook says: “57.9% of global VC dollars invested in Q1 went to AI and machine learning startups.” Most of that’s OpenAI. Even Pitchbook calls it “FOMO” — fear of missing out. [
Pitchbook
]
AI is the only prospect for a lottery-level win. You and I know that’s not going to happen, but the VCs and their customers, the investors, do not know that. They’re still in. Where else are they gonna go?
Everything that isn’t AI is moribund
There’s a world of startups outside AI, a

data.title: A Rust Documentation Ecosystem Review
data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust编程语言生态系统中的文档质量问题，强调了文档对于初学者和专家学习及记忆的重要性。文章指出，尽管程序员往往不喜欢编写文档，但它对于推广库和引导新手至关重要。文章探讨了什么是好的文档，提出了四个衡量标准：全面性、可发现性、设计理念和易接近性。

文章还介绍了Diátaxis框架，该框架将技术文档分为四个象限：教程（tutorials）、操作指南（how-to guides）、技术参考（references）和解释（explanations）。教程注重实践学习，操作指南提供具体问题的解决方案，技术参考详细描述API，解释则阐述设计决策背后的原因。

文章最后对Rust生态系统中多个库的文档进行了评析，强调了改进文档以提高可访问性和用户体验的必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust文档的编写与使用体验

不同观点：
• shepmaster（SNAFU的作者）感谢其crate被纳入评审，并提到正在研究如何将文档框架（如diataxis）应用于SNAFU。他特别关注顶层文档的阅读情况，认为这是主要的介绍材料，而不指望大多数人阅读用户指南。
• theletterf认为文档应该更多关注用户需求，而不是仅仅关注应该写什么内容。他批评了对内容类型的强调，认为这会导致形式化的文档编写，而不是真正满足用户需求。
• airstrike赞赏文章的分析，但指出在docs.rs上浏览crate的困难，常常需要直接查看代码。他特别提到Iced库的文档，认为应该更多地关注如何使用关键概念（如`Element`和`iced::application`），而不是它们的具体实现，以帮助初学者更好地理解。
• xnickb表示不喜欢文章的结论部分，认为其没有提供有用的信息，并习惯在阅读长文之前先看结论以决定是否继续阅读。
• schneems作为crate作者，提到Rust文档不易分享的问题，介绍了一个基于JINJA的解决方案（drydoc），并询问是否有其他类似的工具或方法。

补充讨论：
• airstrike特别欣赏Iced库的简洁设计，例如其初始化应用程序的方式，并建议新手通过"pocket guide"和示例来学习如何使用这些概念。
• schneems提出的drydoc方案虽未完成，但展示了通过模板化来解决Rust文档共享问题的潜力。

争议焦点：
• 文档编写的重点应该是内容类型还是用户需求。theletterf主张以用户需求为中心，而shepmaster和airstrike则更关注具体内容类型的应用和文档结构的合理性。

I’ve been thinking about documentation lately.
Anecdotally, documenting code is somehow one of the least favorite things programmers do. when developing. However, it is undeniable that documentation is essential when it comes to teaching beginners. In fact, one of the most typical ways people can begin their journey in programming is by following a YouTube video tutorial, or reading a book, or tinkering with examples in the “recipe” of your choice. Without such resources (or access to such), less people will be introduced to the field of programming and software development.
Clearly, documentation is important. We read manuals. We read books. We watch video tutorials. And yet, it is an afterthought of a lot of developers, especially those who publish libraries for people to use.
Especially
for people who want such libraries to be popular. Reading documentation is the way for beginners to learn, and the way for experts to remember.
But what constitutes good documentation?
Documentation quality is something that’s not very easy to measure. There are no guidelines to determine whether or not documentation qualifies as satisfactory to the intended audience. However, there are some signs that can tell whether the documentation is
bad
. An obvious example is the
lack
of documentation. How would people understand your library if you don’t have the means to teach it?
There are also other, more
subtle
ways why someone could say the documentation is bad. In newer libraries, the documentation they have is just the API reference. You could glean the meaning of each function and each class and each struct and each record, but the way it can be put together is non-obvious. How do you use so-and-so function? What’s the entry point of this library? Why was this framework architectured this way?
Sometimes, when I don’t see the answer in the documentation. I’ll have to resort to asking people on Discord. I’ll get an answer, I’ll say thank you, and then I don’t think about the Discord server for at least three years. But then, I would think about the next person who would ask the same question, and if they would think twice about using Discord. We have to admit that Discord isn’t an accessible place. It’s a walled garden, and the search functionality is dead. Forums are a much better solution to this, as it has better search indexing and more prominent, but it’s rare to see it in some places.
Ah, discoverability. It’s hard to discover new things without either reading the whole API reference or consume several hundred hours worth of tutorials. Do I need to read the newsletter for each new added feature? Do I need to see some obscure esoteric code in some random Discord channel? There were a lot of cases where people discover and rediscover the
@
syntax
after months of dabbling in Rust and I was kinda surprised, since it was actually discussed in the
Rust Book on the chapter of patterns
. Is the Rust Book not approachable enough?

43953229.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust编程语言生态系统中的文档质量问题，强调了文档对于初学者和专家学习及记忆的重要性。文章指出，尽管程序员往往不喜欢编写文档，但它对于推广库和引导新手至关重要。文章探讨了什么是好的文档，提出了四个衡量标准：全面性、可发现性、设计理念和易接近性。

文章还介绍了Diátaxis框架，该框架将技术文档分为四个象限：教程（tutorials）、操作指南（how-to guides）、技术参考（references）和解释（explanations）。教程注重实践学习，操作指南提供具体问题的解决方案，技术参考详细描述API，解释则阐述设计决策背后的原因。

文章最后对Rust生态系统中多个库的文档进行了评析，强调了改进文档以提高可访问性和用户体验的必要性。

• theletterf认为文档应该更多关注用户需求，而不是仅仅关注应该写什么内容。他批评了对内容类型的强调，认为这会导致形式化的文档编写，而不是真正满足用户需求。
• airstrike赞赏文章的分析，但指出在docs.rs上浏览crate的困难，常常需要直接查看代码。他特别提到Iced库的文档，认为应该更多地关注如何使用关键概念（如`Element`和`iced::application`），而不是它们的具体实现，以帮助初学者更好地理解。

data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 本文总结了Max Rozen运行SaaS产品OnlineOrNot四年来的经验和教训。在竞争激烈的市场中，他坚持了一些核心原则：每天投入两小时、不开展其他副项目、解决客户痛点、持续迭代。他强调阅读少量书籍后就开始实践，通过与客户沟通了解需求，快速发布并不断改进产品。他还分享了一些具体经验，如定价的难度、不盲目扩展产品、不试图解释所有内容以及关注现有流量转化而非仅引入新流量。Rozen认为，竞争对手并不重要，关键是构建可持续的业务并专注于已有成效的策略。通过这些原则和经验，他成功地将OnlineOrNot打造成一个自筹资金、可持续发展的企业。

43909986.article_content:
Four years of running a SaaS in a competitive market
Max Rozen (@RozenMD)
/
April 04, 2025
When I played around with the technology that would eventually become
OnlineOrNot
back in 2021, a quick search showed me that there were 200 listed alternatives to the tool I wanted to replace. I thought most of them sucked.
There are even more today.
Over the years, many more started and shut down a few months later (it turns out running a business in a highly competitive space doesn't make you rich overnight). Others raised VC money or were acquired by a private equity firm, and started their descent into
enshittification
.
I started work on OnlineOrNot because I wanted to build software that didn't have to get worse for its users in order to maximize shareholder value. In short, it's a self-funded, sustainable business that I intend to run for decades.
It's default-alive, as I keep a full time job so that I can build the business the way I want.
I've published one of these articles every year since starting, and there were things that I "learned" in the first year, that turned out to be total bullshit by the third year. So this article doesn't just look at the last 12 months, but across the entire lifetime of this business.
Table of contents:
Principles that haven't changed
Two hours a day, every workday.
No other side projects.
Solve customer pain.
Be ruthlessly iterative.
Lessons
Read a few books, and start building
Solve pain, don't try to sell a subscription
Ship small, ship often
Ship first, worry about scale later
Have an early-access program
Build a free trial as soon as possible
Docs
are
the product
Build for mobile
Ask people how they found you
I don't use invasive analytics
Talk to potential customers, even if you think you have nothing for them
You don't get to spend as much time solving the problem as you think
Pricing is hard to get right
Don't tunnel-vision your MRR
Never give away "unlimited" anything
Rate limit your paid resources
Stop trying to explain everything on one page
It's hard to bring in more traffic, easy to change what your current traffic does
Competitors don't really matter
Principles that haven't changed
While I've learned a lot about running a business over the years, there are some unchanging principles:
Two hours a day, every workday.
Years before I even started OnlineOrNot, I started hacking on my own projects in the two hours I have before starting my workday. Having a consistent block of time for myself has let me publish hundreds of articles, a book, dozens of software projects, and more.
Since starting, I worked out that the amount of time per day isn't as important as putting
any effort
in, every day, for years.
But how do you find time before your workday?
I started waking up two hours earlier, and adjusted the rest of my day accordingly.
No other side projects.
the person who chases two rabbits catches neither
Of course, there are exceptional folks out there chasing a dozen rabbits and managing to catch some of them - I know myself well enough to realize that I'm not that person.
Building out the marketing and sales processes to take a business from $0 to $500 MRR is challenging enough. I don't see a point in repeating the hardest part of starting a business over and over again, instead of doubling down on what's already working (this is also a lesson for picking a marketing approach, more on that later).
Solve customer pain.
When a user signs up for OnlineOrNot, I have an automated email going out asking what brought them to sign up today. I explicitly tell them I read and reply to every email. This is the main source of my insight for building product.
I ask my customers what isn't working, and I make it work.
Be ruthlessly iterative.
If I can't get a piece of work released in two hours, I cut the scope down to something achievable, and iterate on that.
It's worth noting that this is the ideal, and I don't always succeed at cutting down scope to exactly two hours. Over time I've realised that with how my brain works, I enjoy shipping early versions as quickly as possible, and building out the functionality once it's deployed (behind a feature flag).
Waiting until the entire feature is built before deploying completely saps my motivation in comparison, and I find myself easily distracted when building this way.
Lessons
Read a few books, and start building
I read dozens of business books when I wanted to get started, mainly from not wanting to repeat mistakes that others have made.
Sometimes though, you need to make mistakes for yourself.
As an example, it took me getting on the front page of Hacker News, having 6000 people visit my landing page, a few hundred people attempt to sign-up, and only single-digits making it through to the app for me to realise something might be wrong.
I had something like a 75% drop-off rate on my sign-up form alone. I got it down to 50% just by adding an extra OAuth login provider.
If I had to do it all again, I'd start with only three books:

data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在分析实际数据时，简单层次模型与增加更多交互作用的复杂层次模型之间是否需要平衡

不同观点：
• [Onawa] 提出讨论的核心问题：在处理实际数据时，是否需要在简单的层次模型和增加了更多交互作用的复杂模型之间找到平衡。她关注的是模型复杂度的选择以及如何在简单和复杂之间取舍。

• [a-dub] 对Onawa的问题提出了算法化的思路，认为可以从简单的比较开始，逐步增加模型复杂性，直到达到理想的结果。这表明他支持一种循序渐进、逐步增加复杂性的建模方法。

• [joe_the_user] 提出统计模型和机器学习/人工智能模型在目标和方法上的区别。他认为统计模型追求无偏预测，而机器学习模型更关注预测效果，不关心传统意义上的统计偏差。他的观点指向了不同建模范式之间的目标差异，暗示在选择模型时应考虑应用场景和目标。

补充讨论：
• [a-dub] 的观点隐含着对模型选择的实际操作建议，即通过实验和迭代来决定模型的复杂度，而不是一开始就追求最复杂的模型。

• [joe_the_user] 的评论引入了模型类型之间的争议：统计模型和机器学习模型在预测中的不同侧重点。他强调了统计模型在无偏估计上的追求，而机器学习模型则更注重实际预测效果，这可能会影响模型复杂度的选择。

• 争议的焦点在于模型复杂性和目标之间的平衡问题。具体来说，是在统计模型的无偏性与机器学习模型的预测能力之间，如何根据具体应用场景做出选择。

总结来看，讨论围绕着模型复杂度的选择展开，包括如何逐步增加复杂性、统计模型与机器学习模型的不同目标和应用场景，以及如何根据具体需求在这些模型之间做出权衡。

data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: Sansec Forensics团队发现了一场针对电商组件的供应链攻击，涉及Tigren、Magesolution (MGS) 和Meetanshi等多个供应商的21个应用程序被植入后门。该恶意软件在6年前被注入，但直到最近才被激活，攻击者借此控制了大量电商服务器，预计有500至1000家商店受到影响。后门通过伪装成许可证检查的"License.php"或"LicenseApi.php"文件执行，攻击者可利用该漏洞上传恶意文件。建议用户立即检查商店并移除可疑文件，使用Sansec的eComscan进行检测。尽管部分供应商否认被攻击，但后门软件仍在其网站上提供下载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于软件供应商对后门事件的回应及安全漏洞的分析

不同观点：
• BoardsOfCanada 指出几个供应商对后门事件的回应存在问题：Magesolution（MGS）没有回应，但其后门包在4月30日仍可以从其网站下载；Tigren否认被黑客攻击，但其后门包也在其网站上可下载；Meetanshi声称软件未被篡改，但承认服务器确实被入侵。这些回应让人质疑供应商的处理方式和安全性。

• xiphias2 认为这些后门问题似乎与某些Adobe插件（由Adobe商店销售）有关，暗示这些有问题的软件可能通过知名平台传播，增加了问题的严重性。

• blargthorwars 预测，许多潜在的恶意软件载荷将在AI自动检测成为常态之前尽快被激活。虽然AI并不完美，但在检测此类问题上表现良好，暗示未来技术可能有助于缓解当前问题。

• McGlockenshire 从技术角度分析，指出问题可能不仅仅是后门，还可能是远程代码执行（RCE）漏洞。具体提到`adminUploadLicense`功能可以让攻击者控制`licenseFile`，这是一个长期存在的安全隐患，强调了代码中对用户可写文件调用`include`的危险性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于供应商的回应是否充分以及问题的根源是后门还是RCE。BoardsOfCanada对供应商的回应持怀疑态度，而McGlockenshire则从技术细节上提出不同见解，认为问题可能更复杂。

• 讨论还涉及技术发展的影响，如blargthorwars对AI检测的看法，预示着未来技术在网络安全中的作用。

43953723.article_content:
Backdoor found in popular ecommerce components
by Sansec Forensics Team
Published in
Threat Research
− May 01, 2025
Multiple vendors were hacked in a coordinated supply chain attack, Sansec found 21 applications with the same backdoor. Curiously, the malware was injected 6 years ago, but came to life this week as attackers took full control of ecommerce servers. Sansec estimates that between 500 and 1000 stores are running backdoored software.
Hundreds of stores, including a $40 billion multinational, are running backdoored versions of popular ecommerce software. We found that the backdoor is actively used since at least April 20th. Sansec identified these backdoors in the following packages which were published between 2019 and 2022.
Vendor
Package
Tigren
Ajaxsuite
Tigren
Ajaxcart
Tigren
Ajaxlogin
Tigren
Ajaxcompare
Tigren
Ajaxwishlist
Tigren
MultiCOD
Meetanshi
ImageClean
Meetanshi
CookieNotice
Meetanshi
Flatshipping
Meetanshi
FacebookChat
Meetanshi
CurrencySwitcher
Meetanshi
DeferJS
Meetanshi
OutofstockNotifier
MGS
Lookbook
MGS
StoreLocator
MGS
Brand
MGS
GDPR
MGS
Portfolio
MGS
Popup
MGS
DeliveryTime
MGS
ProductTabs
MGS
Blog
We established that Tigren, Magesolution (MGS) and Meetanshi servers have been breached and that attackers were able to inject backdoors on their download servers.
This hack is called a Supply Chain Attack, which is one of the worst types. By hacking these vendors, the attacker gained access to all of their customers' stores. And by proxy, to all of the customers that visit these stores.
We also found a backdoored version of the Weltpixel GoogleTagManager extension, but we have not been able to establish whether Weltpixel or these particular stores got compromised.
Check your store now
If you use software from these vendors, you should check your store now. The backdoor consists of a fake license check in a file called
License.php
or
LicenseApi.php
.
The evil is in the adminLoadLicense function, which executes
$licenseFile
as PHP.
protected
function
adminLoadLicense
(
$licenseFile
)
{
// ...
$data
=
include_once
(
$licenseFile
);
// ...
}
The
$licenseFile
can be controlled by the attacker using the
adminUploadLicense
function. In versions from 2019 this does not require any authentication. In later versions this requires a secret key that must match the hardcoded checksum and salt:
class
License
{
const
SECURE_KEY
=
'83ba291cd9201e9a28173741bac82745'
;
const
SIGN_KEY
=
'afa3a778bd34181c44f2dfe1de8aff05'
;
The fake license check is explicitly activated via
registration.php
.
<?php
\Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar
::
register
(
\Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar
::
MODULE
,
'Meetanshi_CookieNotice'
,
__DIR__
);
if
(
file_exists
(
__DIR__
. DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR .
'Model/System/Config/Source/Box/License/License.php'
)) {
include_once
(
__DIR__
. DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR .
'Model/System/Config/Source/Box/License/License.php'
);
}
The backdoor code is the same for all found packages, except for:
The authorization checksum (unique per vendor)
The backdoor path (unique per module)
The license filename (unique per vendor)
Vendor
Meetanshi
MGS
Tigren
Weltpixel
Secure Key
05aafe4...
83ba291...
e7c057dd...
47946a7...
Sign Key
f31d647...
afa3a77...
313bedf...
52dd8df...
License Filename
mtn-license
mgs-license
apj-license
wlp-license
Recommendations
Sansecâs
eComscan
detects this malware out of the box. If you find a backdoor on your store, you can safely remove the fake License file. If you still have the original source in a zip file (particularly WeltPixel), please
share
it with us for further analysis.
At this point, we recommend to be extremely cautious when using software from these vendors.
Vendor responses
Magesolution (MGS) did not respond, but the backdoored packages can still be downloaded from their site as of Apr 30th.
Tigren denies to have been hacked, but the backdoored packages are still available on their site as of Apr 30th.
Meetanshi claims that their software has not been tampered with, but confirmed that their server got hacked.
Further research
It is rare that a backdoor remains undetected for 6 years, but is even stranger that actual abuse has only started now.
We will update this post when we learn more.

data.title: What the hell are rare earth elements?
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了稀土元素的重要性及其在全球供应链中的战略地位，特别是在电动汽车、智能手机和军事技术等领域。虽然美国曾经在稀土产业占据主导地位，但过去几十年中国逐渐控制了全球约60-70%的稀土开采和高达90%的加工能力。美国在 Mountain Pass 拥有唯一的稀土矿，但依赖中国进行加工和磁材生产。随着中国对稀土出口的限制加剧，美国正努力通过补贴国内加工厂、加快许可审批以及与乌克兰签署矿产投资协议等方式重振稀土产业。尽管稀土并不真正“稀有”，但其提取和加工过程复杂、成本高且对环境有风险，美国面临能否赶超中国的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟稀土元素的定义及相关产业动态，特别是中国和美国在稀土领域的竞争与合作，以及具体稀土元素的例子。

不同观点：
• [thenthenthen] 提到欧盟定义了约30种稀土元素，并引用了欧盟官方来源。他还提到了瑞典通过游戏化方式鼓励当地采矿活动，称之为“矿物狩猎”。但他对未来的发展方向表示不确定。

• [throwaway422432] 回顾了Molycorp公司在20世纪80年代将稀土市场的近垄断地位拱手让给中国的历史，并指出这种模式在多个行业中重复出现。他进一步讨论了Lynas Rare Earths公司在马来西亚的工厂开始生产高稀土元素（如镝和铽），并提到尽管Lynas得到了美国国防部的资助，但其主要客户仍是日本公司如Sumitomo。他还提到Lynas在美国德克萨斯州建设新工厂的计划，但由于废水处理问题，项目成本可能会增加。

• [hkon] 对稀土元素的具体名称感兴趣，并列举了15种稀土元素，但没有深入讨论产业或市场动态。

• [htrp] 提出了一个不同的问题，质疑HubSpot为何经营媒体公司，这与主要讨论点关系不大，但反映了对讨论背景的困惑或不满。

补充讨论：
• 稀土元素的定义和种类在[thenthenthen]和[hkon]的评论中被提及，提供了具体的元素名称和欧盟的定义来源。
• [throwaway422432] 提供了关于稀土产业竞争的历史背景和当前动态的详细信息，特别是中国和美国之间的竞争以及Lynas公司的情况。他还引用了多个来源来支持其论点。
• 争议焦点在于稀土市场的国际竞争和供应链问题，特别是美国和其盟友如何应对中国在这一领域的主导地位。

总体来看，讨论围绕稀土元素的定义、产业动态、历史背景以及国际竞争展开，不同评论者提供了不同的视角和信息。

43953272.article_content:
Rare earths are needed for EVs, smartphones, and fighter jets, but the United States lost the industry to China. Can it win it back?
View in browser
Issue #347
Sunday, May 11, 2025
What the hell are rare earth elements?
Rare earths are needed for EVs, smartphones, and fighter jets, but the United States lost the industry to China. Can it win it back?
BY
MARK DENT
Over the last few weeks, an obscure subject has sowed panic and speculation among investors, the federal government, national security experts, and business leaders:
rare earth elements
.
Commonly called “rare earths,” they encompass 17 elements on the periodic table that are found in underground ore deposits. They’re so useful that rare earths have been referred to as “21st-century gold.”
They help break down petroleum into gasoline, enhance color on TV screens, and can be developed into small
permanent magnets
used in:
Smartphones
Headphones
Electric vehicle motors
F-35 jets
Predator drones
MRI machines
Nuclear submarines
Wind turbines
But for the United States, there’s a problem: China has a stranglehold on rare earths.
China produces
~60-70%
of the world’s mined rare earths and, more importantly, does
~90%
of the world’s processing of rare earths and
~95%
of the production of permanent magnets.
In April, responding to the Trump tariffs, China placed new restrictions on rare earth exports. This adds urgency to US plans for boosting its rare earths sector that started a few years ago and picked up in recent months.
The Pentagon
has subsidized
rare earths processing plants, and a Trump executive order
has attempted
to expedite their permitting. The US also
signed
an investment deal with Ukraine that grants mineral access.
The United States’ only significant rare earth mining facility in Mountain Pass, California. (George Rose/Getty Images)
The good news for the US is rare earths aren’t actually
rare
. The 17 elements are found all over the world. But extracting them, separating and processing them, and developing them into permanent magnets is difficult,
risky for the environment
, and incredibly expensive.
How did the US fall so far behind China in rare earths production? Can it ever catch up?
The Hustle
turned to the rarest of sources for answers:
Jack Lifton
, an 85-year old industry vet who’s a co-founder of the Critical Minerals Institute and has consulted on rare earths for major businesses and countries.
When the United States dominated the rare earths industry
Back in the early 1960s, Lifton started work as a chemical engineer in Detroit, testing out the ultra purification of rare earths in components for integrated circuits.
This was an entirely different era for rare earths: The United States was at the forefront of mining and processing them and enabling technologies for their uses.
The elements were first utilized commercially in the late 19th century to help brighten lamps. Later, rare earths were used as an alloy in ammunition for machine guns.
“When you look at your war movies, and you see those
white tracers
as the machine guns are shooting into the sky, those are rare earth alloys catching fire,” Lifton says.
Olivia Heller/The Hustle
When the industry
picked up
in the 1960s, with rare earths being used as catalysts for refining petroleum and in TV sets, the US had a fortuitous head start.
In the late 1940s in Mountain Pass, California, prospectors Herbert Woodward and Clarence Watkins, had uncovered deposits of bastnasite, a mineral that contains rare earth oxides. The company
Molycorp
purchased claims to the Mountain Pass mine in 1950 and over the next few decades made Mountain Pass, located about 60 miles southwest of Las Vegas, into its own company town.
In addition to mining, Molycorp opened a
large-scale facility for separating the rare earth oxides — one of two in the world when it went on line, Lifton says. This complex process, which was pioneered by researchers in Iowa and can involve hundreds of steps, was necessary to isolate the elements individually so they could be further refined for commercial uses.
In the early 1980s, a breakthrough occurred when General Motors and the Japanese company Sumitomo
developed
a rare earth permanent magnet. GM started making these magnets at commercial scale through an Indiana-based company called Magnequench.
The magnet, derived from the rare earth element
neodymium
, was as strong as an iron magnet but a fraction of the volume, allowing automakers to introduce thin power doors, power steering, and power seats, as well as use permanent magnets in motors. These magnets would prove useful for newer technologies, too.
Olivia Heller/The Hustle
Molycorp rode the wave, increasing its production of rare earth oxides from
~6k metric tons
in the 1960s to more than
20k
by 1990. The company claimed annual revenues between $50m-$100m, and it supplied ~
60%
of the entire world’s rare earths in the early 1980s, according to Lifton.
In other words, the US had the majority of the world’s rare earth pr

data.title: Build iOS Apps on Linux and Windows
data.author: plurby
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在非苹果操作系统（如Linux和Windows）上开发和安装iOS应用，以及对苹果生态封闭性的批评。

不同观点：
• DownrightNifty认为，利用AltStore和SideStore可以在Linux和Windows上安装自制应用，这是对苹果限制的突破，值得推广。这种做法充分利用了我们随身携带的“超级计算机”（指智能手机）的能力。
• bsaul关注是否使用了Swift构建项目，并询问是否遗漏了相关信息，显示出对技术实现细节的关心。
• andrewrn对Linux用户能开发iOS应用感到兴奋，但也提到PWA（渐进式网络应用）在基本应用开发中的能力，并希望更多普通用户了解PWA，而不仅限于从iOS应用商店获取应用。
• weird_trousers对苹果是否会因法律问题（尤其是许可问题）对该项目采取行动表示担忧，但同时对项目的未来表示期待。
• behnamoh批评苹果的封闭生态，指出苹果在产品对比和操作标准上自我中心，不兼容其他操作系统。他还认为，苹果通过限制开发工具和语言（如Swift）来迫使开发者购买Mac设备，是一种企业操纵行为。

补充讨论：
• wmlive提到GNUstep项目提供了类似工具，可以替代Xcode构建iOS软件，提供了另一种技术选择。
• justanotheratom补充说，相关工具也可以在macOS上替代Xcode，并提到一个名为MCP Server的工具用于绕过Xcode。
